01-blog-sourdough.why: Y has a stronger personal voice but invents details like forgetting to feed the starter and having stopped worrying, while X stays close to the original.

02-blog-remote-work.why: X sounds more personal but adds an invented feeling ('that one still bothers me'), while Y adds nothing.

03-blog-product-launch.why: Y is plainer and drops the announcement boilerplate, but X keeps the 'invoicing tool for freelancers' framing more exactly and Y's 'send themselves on a schedule' is a small addition.

04-email-deadline.why: Both keep every fact; X's thanks for flexibility sounds more like a real colleague than Y's blunter wording.

05-email-followup.why: Both keep all the facts; X is tighter, while Y's closing 'keep talking about where we could help' still has some sales filler.

06-email-decline.why: The two are nearly identical and keep every fact; X cuts the formulaic 'I'm honored' line.

07-tech-readme.why: Y adds an unsupported benefit claim ('skips repeated work'); otherwise the two are equivalent.

08-tech-postmortem.why: Y swaps the stock aphorism for a concrete lesson but overstates the impact by saying the outage 'took down checkout' when only 30% of requests failed.

09-tech-pr-description.why: Y adds an invented rationale section ('fits how the vendor delivers events') that the original does not support.

10-essay-cities.why: Y ends on a clear position where X's last line is limp; both keep every fact, with small rewordings of the original's claims.

11-essay-reading.why: X drops the cliched 'window into worlds' opening and the moralizing close, but Y keeps more of the original's claims.

12-essay-ai-art.why: Y keeps a grand closing line about unrealized potential, while X's conclusion is concrete; both keep all four facts.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: Both are faithful; X names the test and ties the cause to the intermittent failures, which reads like a real thread reply.

14-slack-meeting.why: Both keep all three facts; X flows as one natural DM, while Y's first two sentences are slightly choppy.

15-slack-review.why: Y addresses Ken and checks back with him the way a real review reply would; both keep every fact.

16-academic-abstract.why: Y notes the correlational design and drops the causal overclaim, while X still claims that improving sleep could help students perform better.

17-academic-discussion.why: Y hedges the generalizability and reliability claims to match the evidence, while X keeps the 'probably reflect broader trends' overclaim.

18-academic-litreview.why: Both keep all the facts and citations; Y keeps the puffery word 'seminal'.
